newsitem.title: UK: LME option turnover thin ahead of May declaration.
newsitem.headline: LME option turnover thin ahead of May declaration.

text.p: The LME option market was virtually ignored this week, leaving volatility little changed, as a collapse in copper's backwardation stole the limelight, traders said.
Little excitement was expected from next week's options declaration as there were few bulges of open interest at relevant strikes, they added.

But uncertainty in the copper market against a background of ongoing strikes in Chile was likely to make players wary of offloading copper options, usually seen ahead of a long weekend due to time decay.
"I think people will keep what they've got because of the unknown element," a trader said.
Turnover was thin, with total volume in copper options on Wednesday only reaching 3,180 lots.

Looking ahead to next Wednesday's option declaration, traders said most market makers were comfortable with their positions. "Most people are long options and there's not the real interest by those who are short to cover it," a dealer said.

Implied volatility for at-the-money (ATM) copper options were a touch lower compared to the end of last week, with June bid at 17.5 to 18.0 percent, July at 16.5 to 17.0 percent, but the fourth quarter was little changed at 15.5 to 16.0 percent.
Aluminium implied ATM vols on nearby options popped up early in the week, which one trader attributed to short-covering on $1,650 and $1,700 May and June calls.
Another said: "It's a matter of vols being marked up because the market is moving around a bit and seems slightly volatile, but basically it's market makers marking up vols because they are long."
Vols came off on Wednesday after some light granting interest was seen on June and July, and on Thursday, when August was targeted.
Vols on the front months were still slightly firmer compared to last Friday, with June bid at 16.5 to 17.5 percent, July at 16.0 to 17.0 percent and fourth quarter around 15.5 percent.
Zinc and nickel vols were little changed with June zinc bid around 20 percent and June nickel at 22 percent.
